messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High 502/503 rate detected for ELB fleet in eu-central-1 (azb). Error rate > 8% for 5m, latency p95 spiking. Auto-page triggered.
oncall-jen: I’m on it, grabbing pager. What’s the initial scope?
sre-ishaan: seeing 502s from ALBs => backend connection failures to instances in azb. Also Route53 health checks show flapping for a subset of edge prefixes.
netops-marta: Confirmed, we’re seeing asymmetric routing to a few EIPs in azb that only recently reallocated. Possible stale BGP/propagation at edge.
oncall-jen: Can you paste the dashboards?
sre-ishaan: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/ELB/elb-errors?view=azb snapshot attached (log snippet):
```
ELB 502 spike 2026-03-15T09:07:12Z -> backend conn reset from 10.0.4.x, target group tg-xyz unhealthy checks failing
Route53 health: eu-central-edge-1 TTL mismatches, some resolvers still pointing to retired EIP
```
netops-marta: Also seeing increased TCP RSTs on ENI telemetry in azb. Looks post-maintenance leak where EIP reassignment didn’t propagate to all edge routers.
incident-bot: ACTION REQUIRED: Runbook "regional-elb-dns-failover" recommended. Next step: set Route53 weights to divert 70% traffic to eu-west-1.
oncall-jen: I’ll kick the runbook. eng-runtime-dave, can we enable faster failover for these ELBs?
eng-runtime-dave: We can flip ALB target weights and enable cross-zone load balancing more aggressively. Doing controlled weigh shift now.
cs-luke: We have a few customers reporting 502s in eu-central - CS has triaged affected customers and will prepare comms.
prod-comms-amy: Standby for status blurb once we have impact numbers. Keep me in the loop.
sre-ishaan: Executed Route53 weight change (via console) -> new weights: eu-central:30 / eu-west:70. Pushing to AWS; changes may take up to TTL to fully propagate.
netops-marta: Also opened AWS support ticket 1234567890 (BGP/EIP propagation). They're seeing partial EIP table inconsistencies in azb.
oncall-jen: What's the customer impact right now? any major tenants down?
cs-luke: ~12 customers reporting degraded responses, 3 with significant errors (payment / auth). Sent targeted messages to 3 impacted PMs.
eng-runtime-dave: Enabled aggressive retry/backoff on client side for internal routing. Patching proxy configs to accept connections from new frontends.
sre-ishaan: ELB error rate dropped to ~2.1% after weight shift. Latency trending down but still some 5xx from a small subset of backend hosts.
netops-marta: AWS update: "we're reconciling EIP routes; some edge caches still serving stale mappings; mitigation in progress." ETA unknown.
incident-bot: Escalation threshold hit: Incident -> SEV2. Please acknowledge.
oncall-jen: Acknowledged. Assigning follow-on to netops-marta for network mitigation and to sre-ishaan for ELB/backend health.
prod-comms-amy: Draft status: "We are experiencing elevated error rates in eu-central-1. Traffic is being shifted to eu-west-1 and we are working with the cloud provider on root cause. We will update in 30 minutes." Approve? :thinking:
cs-luke: Approved from CS side. Add note about retrying transactions.
eng-runtime-dave: Quick patch: temporarily disable HTTP/2 multiplexing on front proxies for azb paths — reduces backend connection churn. Rolling now to 4/6 proxies.
sre-ishaan: Healthchecks: tg-xyz now 80% healthy, backend reconnections succeeding. Error rate down to 0.9% in last 2m.
netops-marta: AWS confirms propagation will continue; they've forced a route flush in the AZ and seeing fewer stale paths.
oncall-jen: Good. Any remaining customer-impacting symptoms?
cs-luke: One enterprise tenant still seeing intermittent auth failures; working with their SRE on session cookies — seems tied to sticky sessions hitting old backends.
eng-runtime-dave: Adding a temporary cookie-less routing rule to avoid stickiness for sessions from azb. Policy applied.
prod-comms-amy: Updated external status: "Majority of traffic has been re-routed; errors reduced significantly. Some customers in eu-central-1 may see intermittent failures. Investigating." Sent at 09:31 UTC.
incident-bot: Reminder: Take a tidy handoff at +30m.
oncall-jen: I’ll do the on-call rotation handoff at +45. netops-marta, prepare playbook notes for postmortem.
netops-marta: Will collect BGP/EIP diffs, edge router dumps, and AWS support logs.
sre-ishaan: Root-cause hypothesis: EIP reassignment after maintenance didn't fully propagate to edge caches causing asymmetric routing to retired ENIs and backend connection resets -> ALB 502s.
prod-comms-amy: Preparing a single-customer-safe post for public status page. Waiting for final confirmation that action completed.
cs-luke: CS posting targeted follow-ups to the 12 impacted customers now.
eng-runtime-dave: Rolling back the cookie-less rule in 30m if no regressions.
oncall-jen: Current status: incident active, traffic shifted, error rates within SLOs for now. netops and SRE to continue monitoring. Handoff to oncall shift B (sre-ishaan) in 30m.
sre-ishaan: Acknowledged, will take over. I’ll start the timeline notes now.
incident-bot: NOTE: please create JIRA INC-2026-098 for the postmortem and link AWS ticket 1234567890.
prod-comms-amy: Final ping: once we have AWS confirmation of full route reconciliation, I’ll close the external update.
netops-marta: AWS just confirmed full propagation at 09:48 UTC. Edge caches flushed.
sre-ishaan: Verified: ELB error rate steady <0.5% for 10m, latency normal. Marking mitigation complete.
oncall-jen: Excellent. Closing out immediate mitigation. Next steps: postmortem, follow-up with AWS for preventive controls, runbook updates to include forced EIP route flush step.
cs-luke: CS will coordinate customer follow-ups and impact summaries.
prod-comms-amy: External status updated to "Resolved" at 09:52 UTC with post-incident note to follow.
sre-ishaan: Adding timeline entries and recording for postmortem. I’ll own the write-up.
oncall-jen: Handoff complete. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
